services.intro: 24 services in four groups, from a furnace that won't light to a restaurant's make-up air unit.

price.intro: We don't publish a price book, and we're not going to invent one here. What we can show you is what moves the number.
price.medianCaption: Median reported value of 81 central-furnace replacement permits in Chicago over 24 months. That's the whole project's construction value, not a quote.

choose.lede: Ask them of anyone you call, including us.

questions.title: Who diagnoses, and who quotes?
questions.text: If they're different people, ask who owns the outcome. Here it's Rob for both.

questions.title: Is the technician on commission?
questions.text: Commission on replacements changes what "your furnace is done" means.

questions.title: Does a permit count mean anything here?
questions.text: Not for repairs. Chicago doesn't permit HVAC repair or maintenance, so a permit count only measures installs.

questions.title: What do the newest reviews say?
questions.text: Read the last 20, not the top 5. Look for names and specifics.

questions.title: Will they tell you to keep it?
questions.text: Ask if the unit has years left. Our reviewers record hearing "yes".

companies.heading: Who you'll meet, and what limits each of them

items.title: Family-owned, since 1952
items.text: The owner answers and quotes. Limit: one family's capacity, so peak-winter days fill up.

items.title: National franchise
items.text: Response time is genuinely good. Limit: commission and price books shape the recommendation.

items.title: One-van independent
items.text: The work is often excellent. Limit: one person, so a January no-heat call can wait days.

items.title: Lead marketplace
items.text: Several quotes fast. Limit: you don't choose who calls back, or who turns up.

about.heading: Who you're actually calling?
about.ownerTile: Owner-operator. He runs the calls himself, so the person who quotes is the person accountable.
about.foundedTile: 74 years, family owned, now in its second generation.
about.permitTile: Permits on record. Chicago doesn't permit HVAC repair, which is most of what we do.

promises.title: The owner on the call
promises.text: Rob still runs the calls and does the diagnosis on the jobs that need it.

promises.title: Repair first
promises.text: If the unit has years left, we say so and repair it.

promises.title: The price before the work
promises.text: You hear the price before any work starts.

reviews.heading: Why Chicago homeowners keep calling the same family
reviews.intro: Quoted word for word from Google, never edited. Several reviewers were told their old unit still had years left.

process.heading: From the first call to a warm apartment, in six steps

steps.title: You call, Rob listens
steps.text: Tell us the make of the furnace or condenser and what it's doing. A good description often narrows it down on the phone.

steps.title: Pick a time
steps.text: We're available 24/7. If your building has rules on access, like elevator or work hours, tell us and we book around them.

steps.title: On-site diagnosis
steps.text: The technician finds the actual fault: ignition, pressure, refrigerant, airflow or controls.

steps.title: Honest price, repair first
steps.text: You hear the price before any work. If the unit has years left, we say so and repair it.

steps.title: We fix it
steps.text: Repairs done on the spot where the part is on the van. Installs are scheduled and quoted separately.

steps.title: Good to go
steps.text: The system is tested through a full cycle before we leave, and you know what to watch for.

permits.heading: Why you won't find us in the City's permit file
permits.text: Chicago doesn't require a permit to repair, diagnose or maintain heating and cooling, which is most of what we do. The permit file measures construction, not service. So when a company waves a permit count at you, ask how much of their work is repair.
permits.citywideCaption: Firms that pull HVAC permits citywide, across 4,888 permits in 24 months.
permits.ourCaption: Permits on record for City & Suburban. We said we'd be honest.

items.question: Does HVAC repair in Chicago need a permit?
items.answer: No. Chicago doesn't require a permit to repair, diagnose or maintain heating and cooling. Permits cover installs and construction, so a company's permit count says little about its repair work.
